name: airgorah
one_liner: A point-and-click app for testing how secure a WiFi network actually is, instead of typing raw command-line hacking tools by hand.
buyer: A freelance penetration tester or small security consultancy that audits client WiFi networks and wants an easy GUI tool instead of juggling command-line tools.
business_use_cases: A freelance pentester uses it during an authorized client engagement to demonstrate how easily a weak WiFi password can be captured and cracked, as evidence in the audit report.
A security consultancy trains junior staff on WiFi auditing with its GUI before they move on to raw command-line tools.

money_ideas.idea: No direct monetization of the tool itself; the money comes from the paid pentesting or audit engagement it supports

steal_this: This isn't really a weekend product play on its own — the honest move is bundling it into a $500 flat-fee 'WiFi security audit for small offices' service you already know how to deliver, and only on networks you're authorized to test.
